title: Private Deploy Artifact Distribution & Upgrade Verification Protocol (PRD)
creator: Aisha Patel
overview: Define a reproducible, verifiable protocol for distributing Redwood runtime artifacts (images, manifests, delta patches) to Private/VPC deployments that may be air-gapped or have constrained egress. The protocol must enable deterministic verification, allow staged rollouts, support mirror-based pull models, and provide explicit acceptance criteria for upgrades and rollback validation.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private frequently operate in environments with restricted egress, strict change-control, and audit requirements. Current ad-hoc artifact distribution flows rely on manual mirroring or temporary egress windows; we need a standardized protocol that reduces operational burden while meeting security and upgrade-safety SLAs.
objectives: Specify artifact packaging and manifest formats that support signature and provenance verification without requiring internet connectivity
Define allowed transport mechanisms (S3 signed URLs, internal mirrors, physical media ingestion) and a single verification flow consumed by the Private control-plane
Formalize upgrade verification checks (schema/cert checks, delta checksum validation, preflight smoke tests) and rollout gating logic for zero-downtime and safe rollback
Minimize required egress surface and make offline validation deterministic for audits
non_goals: We will not design a new PKI; we will rely on existing KMS/HSM and image signing tools (Cosign or equivalent),
We will not change hosted API behavior or runtime internals unrelated to artifact distribution
We will not implement a custom physical media courier service (customers may use their own channels)
requirements: R1: Artifact manifest SHALL include: semantic version, image digests, delta patch metadata (optional), signed manifest (RFC-compliant), and a provenance URL. Manifest format: JSON with strict schema v1.0.

R2: All artifacts and manifests MUST be signed with a customer- or Redwood-trusted signing key. The control plane MUST be able to verify signatures offline using pinned public keys or provided certificate bundles.

R3: Artifact transport options supported: direct registry pull, pre-seeded OCI mirror, S3-compatible mirror (signed temporary URLs), and manual ingestion via tarball. The control plane MUST support configuration for multiple mirror endpoints and fallbacks.
R4: Upgrade orchestration MUST support canary percentages, staged rollouts, and automatic rollback triggers when verification or smoke tests fail.

R5: Preflight verification steps before marking an upgrade as successful: signature verification, digest checksum match, container image unpack sanity check, runtime preflight smoke tests (start/health-check), and KV cache warm start check for stateful components.
R6: For air-gapped installs where registry access is blocked, the control plane MUST accept an explicit mirror manifest containing local mirror mapping and a signed bundle of the artifacts.

R7: Upgrade operations MUST generate a deterministic audit record including manifest digest, signer identity, time, operator identity, and outcome; records must be exportable to customer SIEM or stored in the control plane audit log.
R8: Rollback MUST be possible to the previous successful manifest with immutability guarantees; if delta patches were applied, full-image fallback MUST be supported.

R9: Minimal runtime egress policy for non-air-gapped installs: single outbound connection to validation endpoint (TLS) to fetch CRL/OCSP and optional telemetry; must be configurable and document default domains/ports.
R10: Validation tooling (CLI or UI) SHALL be provided to confirm mirror health, manifest integrity, and preflight checks prior to scheduling upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Given a signed manifest and image bundle hosted on an internal mirror, the Private control plane performs full signature and digest verification without reaching the public internet and reports success in the UI and audit log.

AC-2: For air-gapped flow, an operator provides a signed bundle (tar.gz) and a mirror manifest; the control plane imports the artifacts, validates signatures, and lists them as available images for rollout.

AC-3: When a canary rollout is configured (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with smoke tests enabled, any smoke test failure causes automatic rollback to the last successful manifest and emits a rollback audit entry with a reason and traceback.

AC-4: In the presence of a corrupted artifact (mismatched checksum), upgrade is blocked and the UI surfaces a clear failure state with remediation steps; remediation may include re-syncing the mirror or re-uploading signed artifacts.

AC-5: The system exports a per-upgrade audit record (JSON) including manifest_digest, signer_key_id, operator, timestamps, preflight_results, smoke_test_results, and final_status; exported records match the signed manifest digest and are consumable by customer SIEMs.

AC-6: The validation CLI can run in offline mode against a local mirror, produce a signed validation report, and the control plane can ingest this report as optional evidence to fast-track upgrades under restricted egress policies.

AC-7: Rollback works for both delta-patch and full-image upgrades; after rollback, the cluster returns to previous health baseline within the defined SLA window (default 10 minutes for control-plane services).
upgrade_flow: 1) Operator prepares signed manifest and artifacts. 2) Operator uploads to chosen mirror or provides bundle. 3) Control plane imports manifest and verifies signatures/offline checks. 4) Preflight verification runs on a designated canary subset. 5) Staged rollout proceeds per policy; any failed preflight or smoke test triggers automated rollback and an incident entry. 6) On success, control plane marks manifest as deployed and emits audit/telemetry.
test_plan: TP1: Automated E2E: simulate internal mirror with intentionally corrupted blob to assert blocking behavior and error messages.
TP2: Air-gap bundle test: ingest signed tarball into clean private cluster and validate artifact import, preflight, and canary rollout.
TP3: Canary rollback test: run staged rollout with injected failure in smoke test target and confirm rollback event, audit record, and restored health.
TP4: Validation CLI offline-run test: ensure the CLI generates a signed validation report the control plane accepts and treats as equivalent to online verification when configured.
TP5: Audit export test: export per-upgrade JSON to an S3 target and validate schema and fields against customer SIEM ingestion.
TP6: Networking constraints test: verify minimal egress configuration suffices for non-air-gapped installs; document ports/domains required and provide a hardened policy file.
risks: RISK-1: Customers may mis-manage signing keys leading to blocked upgrades; mitigate with clear key rotation docs and a recovery path using operator-approved overrides.
RISK-2: Mirror inconsistencies could cause partial upgrades; mitigate by requiring manifest-level digests and by offering a preflight mirror-consistency check tool.
RISK-3: Offline verification introduces complexity for runtime telemetry and crash reporting; document limitations and provide opt-in telemetry with explicit customer consent.
RISK-4: Large customers may have proprietary transport tooling that doesn't match our manifest model; provide integration hooks and a reference importer.
dependencies: ENG-4521: Control-plane manifest verification library (Cosign integration)
ENG-4988: Mirror configuration API and multiple endpoint support
ENG-5015: Validation CLI and signed report ingestion
SEC-210: Key management and signing operational runbook
DOCS-301: Customer upgrade runbooks and minimal-egress policy guide
rollout_notes: Phase 1: internal dogfood in hardened VPC with simple mirror. Phase 2: pilot with two enterprise customers (one air-gapped, one low-egress). Phase 3: general availability with docs, validation CLI, and audit export. Provide migration guide and default policy templates. Monitor early rollouts for false positives in signature verification and adjust error messaging for operator clarity.
